problem_solving.exam_focus: GMAT Problem Solving questions test quantitative reasoning in business contexts
problem_solving.question_topics: Algebra, Geometry, Number Theory, Arithmetic, Data Analysis, Statistics, Logical Reasoning, Word Problems, Probability, Combinatorics, Advanced Topics
problem_solving.focused_skills: Attention to Detail, Logical Reasoning, Critical Reasoning, Mathematical Knowledge, Efficiency and Time Management

vocabulary_requirements.business_context: All questions must include realistic business scenarios
vocabulary_requirements.complexity_scaling: Increase business scenario complexity with difficulty level

question_categories.arithmetic: Critical reasoning, number sense, avoiding common pitfalls - Topics: Ratio/proportion, discount/profit/loss, rates, unitary method
question_categories.algebra: Back-solving capability, strategic number picking - Topics: Equations, inequalities, functions, polynomials
question_categories.word_problems: Situation assessment, step setup, tool selection - Business contexts with complex scenarios requiring multiple steps

difficulty_scaling.level_1: Minimum 3 calculation steps, straightforward business context
difficulty_scaling.level_2: Minimum 5 steps, moderate complexity with business terminology
difficulty_scaling.level_3: 5+ steps with confusing wording and business jargon
difficulty_scaling.level_4: 7+ steps, multiple concepts, advanced business scenarios
difficulty_scaling.level_5: 10+ steps, trial-and-error reasoning, highly complex business operations

json_format.error_handling: Retry with format warnings if JSON parsing fails

data_sufficiency.exam_focus: GMAT Data Sufficiency questions focus on logical reasoning and mathematical analysis
data_sufficiency.question_topics: Algebra, Geometry, Number Theory, Arithmetic, Data Analysis, Statistics, Logical Reasoning, Word Problems, Probability, Combinatorics, Advanced Topics
data_sufficiency.focused_skills: Attention to Detail, Logical Reasoning, Critical Reasoning, Mathematical Knowledge, Efficiency and Time Management
data_sufficiency.complexity_requirements: Make statements more complex and confusing to make question more difficult
data_sufficiency.business_context: Questions should reflect business and management scenarios where appropriate

critical_reasoning.exam_focus: GMAT Critical Reasoning tests business judgment and logical analysis
critical_reasoning.question_categories: Weaken the argument, strengthen the argument, find the assumption, draw inference/conclusion, structure of the argument, paradox, evaluate the conclusion, complete the argument
critical_reasoning.business_context: Questions should focus on business scenarios, management decisions, and corporate strategy
critical_reasoning.difficulty_scaling: Higher difficulty levels should include complex business scenarios and sophisticated logical reasoning
critical_reasoning.variations: Boldface Questions, Cause and Effect, Plan and Outcome

reading_comprehension.exam_focus: GMAT Reading Comprehension emphasizes business and academic passages
reading_comprehension.passage_types: Business strategy, economics, science, social sciences, humanities
reading_comprehension.question_types: Main idea, supporting details, inference, author's tone, structure
reading_comprehension.business_context: Include passages about business management, organizational behavior, and market analysis

graphic_interpretation.exam_focus: GMAT Integrated Reasoning tests data interpretation and analysis skills
graphic_interpretation.business_context: Use business-relevant data such as sales, revenue, market share, performance metrics
graphic_interpretation.difficulty_scaling: Difficulty levels 4 and 5 require multiple related graphs for complex analysis

table_analysis.exam_focus: GMAT Table Analysis tests data sorting and analysis capabilities
table_analysis.business_context: Use business data tables with financial, operational, or market information
table_analysis.table_requirements: Dynamic table size based on difficulty (rows: difficulty + 5-7, cols: difficulty + 3-5)

two_part_analysis.exam_focus: GMAT Two-Part Analysis tests multi-step reasoning and analysis
two_part_analysis.business_context: Questions should involve business decisions requiring two related determinations
two_part_analysis.question_structure: Shared content with two related questions that test different aspects

multi_source_reasoning.exam_focus: GMAT Multi-Source Reasoning tests synthesis of information from multiple sources
multi_source_reasoning.source_types: Text, tables, graphs combined to create comprehensive business scenarios
multi_source_reasoning.business_context: Use business case studies with multiple data sources requiring integrated analysis
